estimated.text: 这次 deck_context 预计花 6 点、3 条出站请求，在硬顶之内。

cost.note: This backend needs no quota (off-network rule).

data.howto: Confirm the workspace and the backend with this tool before you write a ticket. Create tickets with deck_issue_create, a whole map skeleton with deck_map_plan_create, extra edges with deck_map_link, changes to a ticket with deck_issue_patch, the ticket you are working on with deck_issue_report, one ticket with deck_issue_get, every sub-issue of a map with deck_map_snapshot, and thin rows by state, label and assignee with deck_issue_list. To spend fewer points: scan with deck_issue_list thin rows first; for the reverse edges of one ticket, when you are not in a hurry, call deck_issue_get with blocking=false (it skips one whole-repo scan); when the list of sub-issues must be full and unbroken, call deck_map_snapshot with detail=thin (the counts stay the same). The workspace and the repo take no arguments: they come from the current session only. Everything the user types themselves is worth recording in the original words section of that ticket: when creating or changing a ticket, pass {text,source} in originalWords, unchanged and append-only; the original words on a ticket are the highest requirement for that ticket, and where the rest of the ticket conflicts with them the original words win, so if you cannot tell, tell the user there is a clear conflict. To see which sessions are working on which tickets, and whether anyone is competing with you for the same ticket, call deck_work_route; running:true on a group means that session really has a turn open at this moment (waiting for approval or for an answer counts too). One more creation contract for the local backend: tickets and specs are Markdown files in the workspace, and where they are written and what they look like is decided only by the bundled skill text setup-matt-pocock-skills/issue-tracker-local.md: a spec is .scratch/<feature-slug>/spec.md; an exploration map is .scratch/<effort>/map.md; a spec ticket, a map ticket and a plain ticket are all .scratch/<effort>/issues/<NN>-<slug>.md, one ticket per file. Create tickets with deck_issue_create: kind=spec creates a spec, kind=map creates an exploration map, kind=spec-ticket with parentKey creates a spec ticket (put dependencies in blockedBy), kind=map-ticket with parentKey creates a map ticket (parentKey is the exploration map, label is one of wayfinder:research / wayfinder:prototype / wayfinder:grilling / wayfinder:task), and kind=issue and kind=bug create plain tickets and bug tickets; the tool writes the number and the hidden header comments, so do not write ticket files by hand. Add edges with deck_map_link, and change a ticket, assign it or change its state with deck_issue_patch: the tool maintains the field lines and the hidden comments in the layout of the skill text, so do not edit them yourself. Where the skill text conflicts with this usage note, the skill text wins. Reporting is bookkeeping: deck_issue_report only records one line and carries no board, so to see which sessions are working on which tickets call deck_work_route (by default it shows only what moved in the last 24 hours; pass includeStale:true to see the last 30 days).
